..Title
Authorizing the appropriation and expenditure of $26,430 from the Water Replacement Fund for the purchase of pressure compensators from the original equipment manufacturer of the high-pressure pumps in the Solids Dewatering Facility at the Collins Park Water Treatment Plant; waiving the competitive procurement provisions under TMC Chapter 187; and declaring an emergency.

..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
      Universal Filtration & Pumping Solutions, Inc. is the exclusive North American distributor for EMS, the original equipment manufacturer of the high-pressure pumps that are installed in the Solids Dewatering Facility at the Collins Park Water Treatment Plant (CPWTP). The Solids Dewatering Facility is a critical process in cost effectively handling the spent lime that is a byproduct of the treatment process at Collins Park. The Division of Water Treatment is seeking a contract with Universal Filtration & Pumping Solutions, Inc. in the amount of $26,430 for the purchase of pressure compensators in order to improve operational efficiency, throughput and reliability of the dewatering process at the CPWTP Solids Dewatering Facility. Funds are available in the Water Replacement Fund.  

..Summary
NOW, THEREFORE, Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

      SECTION 1.	That the appropriation of $26,430 is authorized from the unappropriated balance of the Water Replacement Fund to Account Code 6063-32000-4UC0624STDSTD for the purchase of pressure compensators for the high-pressure dewatering pumps at the CPWTP; and the expenditure of the same is authorized.

      SECTION 2.	That the Mayor is authorized to enter into a contract with Universal Filtration & Pumping Solutions, Inc. for the purchase of pressure compensators for the high-pressure dewatering pumps at the CPWTP, upon terms and conditions approved by the Director of Public Utilities and the Director of Law.

      SECTION 3.  That this Council finds and determines that it is in the best interest of the City to waive the competitive procurement provisions of TMC Chapter 187 for the reason that sole-source equipment standardization is critical for operation continuity and equipment availability within the Solids Dewatering Facility at the CPWTP and for the further reason of reducing the cost of spent lime disposal and reuse.

      SECTION 4. That the Finance Director is authorized to issue their warrant or warrants against the account code identified in Section 1 in an amount not to exceed $26,430 in payment of the obligations authorized above upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers.
      
	SECTION 5. That this Ordinance is declared to be an emergency measure and shall take effect and be in force from and after its passage. The reason for the emergency lies in the fact that this Ordinance is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety and property, and for the further reason that this Ordinance must be immediately effective in order to improve the operational efficiency, throughput and reliability of the dewatering process at the CPWTP.

..Title
Authorizing the expenditure of $500,000 from the Sewer Replacement Fund for the Plant Electrical Motors & Actuators Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Bay View Water Reclamation Plant; waiving the competitive bidding provisions of TMC Chapter 187 for proprietary parts and equipment replacement; authorizing the Mayor to accept bids and award contracts necessary for the Project; and declaring an emergency.

..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
The Bay View Water Reclamation Plant houses the wastewater treatment facilities which can handle up to 195 million gallons per day, and the wet weather treatment facilities which can handle up to 205 million gallons per day. The Plant as well as the outside pump stations employ numerous electrical motors, actuators and other related equipment to power and drive various equipment and treatment systems. Currently, the conditions of many electrical motors and actuators are of great concern, which upon failure could adversely affect the operational integrity of the treatment systems. 

The Division of Water Reclamation intends to seek formal and informal cost proposals to rebuild and/or replace electrical motors, actuators and other related equipment in order to maintain compliance with Ohio EPA's National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) discharge permit, and to provide the necessary redundancy of such equipment as needed. Some equipment may require proprietary parts for rebuild and others can only be purchased from sole sources when needed. For that, the Division is requesting a waiver of all competitive bidding provisions of TMC Chapter 187.
      
..Summary
NOW THEREFORE Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

      SECTION 1. That the expenditure of $500,000 is authorized from the Sanitary Sewer Replacement Fund Account Code 6073-36000-4UC0623STDSTD for the rebuild and/or replacement of electrical motors, actuators and other related equipment in order to facilitate the Plant Electrical Motors & Actuators Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Bay View Water Reclamation Plant.

      SECTION 2. That the Mayor is authorized to accept bids and award contracts for equipment rebuild, equipment replacement and for professional, engineering, permitting, testing and construction services necessary for the completion of the Plant Electrical Motors & Actuators Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Bay View Water Reclamation Plant, upon terms and conditions approved by the Director of Public Utilities and the Director of Law.

      SECTION 3.  That this Council finds and determines it is in the best interest of the City to waive the competitive procurement provisions of TMC Chapter 187 for equipment rebuild and replacement from sole sources, and for the further reason that electrical equipment standardization is critical for equipment availability and operation continuity at the Bay View Water Reclamation Plant.

      SECTION 4. That the Finance Director is authorized to issue their warrant or warrants against the Account Code identified in Section 1 in an amount not to exceed $500,000 in payment of the authorized obligations upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers. 

      SECTION 5. That the disappropriation of any remaining budget to fund balance is authorized at project closeout.

	SECTION 6. That this Ordinance is declared to be an emergency measure and shall take effect and be in force from and after its passage. The reason for the emergency lies in the fact that this Ordinance is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety and property, and for the further reason that this Ordinance must be immediately effective in order to facilitate the Plant Electrical Motors & Actuators Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Bay View Water Reclamation Plant.

..Title
Authorizing the expenditure of an amount not to exceed $25,000 from the Water Operating Fund for emergency repair services to the Low Service Pumping Station air conditioners; authorizing the Mayor to enter into a contract for said purpose; and declaring an emergency.

..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
The project is at the City of Toledo's Low Service Pumping Station where the division draws water from Lake Erie. The speed of the four 1400 HP pumps, used one or more at a time combination to deliver water to the plant, is controlled by four variable frequency drives (VFDs). The VFDs generate a significant amount of heat and are in their own room. The room includes two Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC) units that operate as needed to keep the VFDs cool. One of the CRAC units has failed and work on units this size is beyond the certification level of skilled trades employed by the City. During summer months one CRAC unit alone cannot maintain the room temperature below 80 degrees F, the maximum allowable ambient room temperature. Lead time on the compressors is 24 weeks, and it is uncertain when compressors on the other unit may fail. If the pumps cannot operate due to excessive heat, the City of Toledo and surrounding communities could be without water.

..Summary
NOW THEREFORE Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

      SECTION 1.	That the expenditure of an amount not to exceed $25,000 from the Water Operating Fund is authorized from Account Code 6060-32000-4000505STDSTD for emergency repair services at the Low Service Pumping Station. 
      
      SECTION 2. That the Mayor is authorized to enter into a contract for emergency repair services for the VFD room air conditioning units at the Low Service Pumping Station, upon terms and conditions approved by the Director of Public Utilities and the Director of Law. 

      SECTION 3. That the Finance Director is authorized to issue their warrant or warrants against the Account Code identified in Section 1 in an amount not to exceed $25,000 in payment of the obligations authorized above upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers. 

      SECTION 4. That this Ordinance is declared to be an emergency measure and shall take effect and be in force from and after its passage. The reason for the emergency lies in the fact that this Ordinance is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety and property, and for the further reason that this Ordinance must be immediately effective in order to complete emergency repair services related to the air conditioning units at Low Service Pump Station.

..Title
Authorizing the expenditure of $26,000 from the Sewer Operating Fund for the purchase of bar screen parts from the original equipment manufacturer for the Bay View Pump Station; waiving the competitive procurement provisions of TMC Chapter 187; and declaring an emergency.

..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
Bar screens at the Bay View Wastewater Treatment Plant filter out large solid objects such as rags, plastics, paper, and other materials from the incoming wastewater. These materials would otherwise not be broken down by the treatment processes and would result in the plugging up of pumps and/or increased wear of the pumps. Either of these conditions would lead to the Plant not being able to treat all of the incoming wastewater.  Headworks, Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer and sole source of replacement for bar screen parts at the Bay View Wastewater Plant. The parts are proprietary and patented, and the purchase of the parts must be done through their Ohio authorized sales representative, BL Anderson, Inc. The Division of Water Reclamation is seeking a contract with BL Anderson, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $26,000 for the purchase of parts necessary to repair the bar screens in order to maintain efficient operation of the Plant and protect downstream equipment. Funds are available in the Sewer Operating Fund.

..Summary

	SECTION 1. 	That the expenditure of $26,000 is authorized from the Sewer Operating Fund Account Code 6070-36000-4000507STDSTD for the purchase of bar screen parts for the Bay View Pump Station.

      SECTION 2.	That the Mayor is authorized to enter into a contract with BL Anderson, Inc. for the purchase of bar screen parts for the Bay View Pump Station, upon terms and conditions approved by the Director of Public Utilities and the Director of Law.

      SECTION 3.       SECTION 4. That the Finance Director is authorized to issue their warrant or warrants against the account code identified in Section 1 in an amount not to exceed $26,000 in payment of the obligations authorized above upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers.

The project takes place at the City of Toledo's Spentlime Dewatering Facility, where spentlime is processed into a reusable solid form. The facility operates two presses, handling approximately 250,000 gallons of spentlime per day. The spentlime entering the presses has a solid content of 4-5%, which increases to 45-50% after processing. A mixer is used to keep solids suspended; if the mixer malfunctions, the solids content drops to about 3-4% before pressing. Higher solid content going into the presses results in a higher percentage of solids coming out. Currently, only one mixer is in operation, and there is no functional spare available if it fails.

..Summary
NOW THEREFORE Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

	SECTION 1. That the Mayor is authorized to enter into a one (1) year agreement with Buckeye Pumps for the purpose of repair services for the Spentlime Dewater Facility pre-fill tank mixer, located at the Collins Park Water Treatment Plant, upon terms and conditions acceptable to the Department of Public Utilities and the Director of Law.

      SECTION 3. ..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
The Bay View Water Reclamation Plant (Plant) has four anaerobic digesters in service. The temperature of the sludge inside the anaerobic digesters must be kept around 95 F for proper operation. Each digester is served by a heat exchanger that is used to transfer heat from the circulating hot water to the circulating digester sludge. Maintaining proper temperatures is imperative for the biological breakdown of solids and for the production of methane gas. Two out of four heat exchangers were replaced three years ago with funds approved under Ordinance No. 255-22. The other two heat exchangers are over 35 years of age and have been breaking down resulting in lower operating temperatures in the corresponding digesters. It is now necessary to replace the two old heat exchangers. A proper operation of the digester system is crucial for sludge digestion and is required by the Plant's National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) discharge permit. The Division of Water Reclamation (Division) will prepare a Request for Proposals (RFP) and advertise for the replacement of the two old heat exchangers. The Division intends to use the remaining funds from Ordinance No. 255-22, but will need an additional amount of $100,000 to complete the project.

Settled sludge is removed from each Final Settling Tank by a hydraulic sludge collector. Each sludge collector is driven by a 0.5 horsepower drive unit located at the center of the tank. The settled sludge collector for Final Settling Tank #2 is currently inoperable due to a defective drive unit. Windermere Pump Station (Improvement 68), is a high priority project of the Program and is ready to move to final design and construction.   

The Division has decided to implement this project using the Progressive Design Build (PDB) delivery method as allowed under Ohio Revised Code Sections 153.501-153.503 and 153.65-153.72, and Ohio Administrative Code Section 153:1.  PDB projects involve hiring a design-builder to design the project and then proceed directly into construction, which can result in cost and schedule savings compared to the typical design-bid-build process.  In accordance with the ORC, the Division issued a Request for Qualifications on December 5, 2025 and subsequentially qualified the three submitting firms to submit detailed proposals on April 21, 2026.   The Division’s Selection Committee reviewed the three proposals and is recommending proceeding with Mosser Construction, Inc.  This Ordinance will authorize entering into a loan agreement with the Ohio EPA Water Pollution Control Loan Fund and Ohio Water Development Authority and appropriating loan proceeds in an amount of $1,671,459 to cover pre-construction (design) services.


..Summary
NOW THEREFORE Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

SECTION 1. That the Mayor is authorized to enter into agreements, and accept a loan from the Ohio EPA Water Pollution Control Loan Fund (WPCLF) and the Ohio Water Development Authority (OWDA) and to deposit loan proceeds in an amount not to exceed $1,671,459 into the Sanitary Sewer Replacement Fund, Account Code 673L-36000-4UL2526STDSTD, for Windermere Pump Station Improvements (Improvement 68).

SECTION 3.  That an amount not to exceed $1,671,459 is appropriated from the unappropriated loan proceeds in the Sanitary Sewer Replacement Fund into Account Code 673L-36000-4UL2526STDSTD; and further authorizing the expenditure of the same amount for Improvement 68.

SECTION 4.	That the Mayor is authorized to accept bids and award contracts for Improvement 68 using the Progressive Design Build delivery method as provided for by Ohio Revised Code Sections 153.501-153.503 and 153.65-153.72, and Ohio Administrative Code Section 153:1, upon such terms and conditions as shall be approved by the Director of Public Utilities and the Director of Law.

SECTION 5.	That the dedicated source of repayment for said loan shall be the unappropriated balance of the Sanitary Sewer Replacement Fund provided, however, that any loan for this project shall be subordinate to all of the City’s sanitary sewer revenue bonds.

SECTION 6.  That the Director of Finance is authorized to issue their warrant or warrants against the Account Code identified above in an amount not to exceed $1,671,459 in payment of the above-authorized obligations upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers.

SECTION 7.  That this Ordinance is declared to be an emergency measure and shall be in force and effect from and after its passage.  The reason for the emergency lies in the fact that same is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety and property, and for the further reason that this Ordinance must be immediately effective in order to maintain the operational integrity of the Water Reclamation Facility, and to maintain compliance with the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System discharge permit requirements, as set forth by the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency.

..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
The Water Reclamation Facility houses both a traditional activated sludge treatment facility and a wet weather treatment facility which have a combined total treatment capacity of 400 million gallons of sewage per day. The treatment facility and the collection system, including pump stations contains hundreds of pumps, valves, gates, motors, actuators, etc. In order to maintain compliance with our National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), this equipment needs to be maintained, repaired, and replaced as needed. The Division intends to seek formal as well as informal proposals for rebuilding and/or replacing pumps, valves, gates, motors, actuators, and other equipment as needed in order to maintain compliance with the NPDES discharge permit and to provide the necessary redundancy of such equipment at the facility and throughout the collection system. Some equipment will require the purchase of proprietary parts for repair or rebuild and others can only be purchased from authorized sole sources. For that, the Division is requesting a waiver of all competitive bidding provisions of TMC Chapter 187. 

..Summary
NOW THEREFORE Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

SECTION 1. That the appropriation of $300,000 from the unappropriated balance of the Sewer Replacement Fund is authorized to Account Code 6073-36000-4UC2726STDSTD for the completion of the Plant Pumps, Motors & Valves Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Water Reclamation Facility; and the expenditure of the same is authorized.

SECTION 2. That the Mayor is authorized to accept bids and award contracts for equipment rebuilds, equipment replacement and for professional, engineering, permitting, testing and construction services necessary for the completion of the Plant Pumps, Motors & Valves Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Water Reclamation Facility, upon terms and conditions approved by the Director of Public Utilities and the Director of Law. 

SECTION 3. That this Council finds and determines when necessary, it is in the best interest of the City to waive all competitive bidding provisions of TMC Chapter 187 for equipment rebuilds with proprietary parts or equipment replacement from authorized sole sources.

SECTION 4. That the Finance Director is authorized to issue warrant or warrants against the Account Code listed in Section 1 in the amount of $300,000 in payment of the above authorized obligations upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers.

SECTION 5.  That the disappropriation of any remaining budget to fund balance is authorized at project closeout.

	SECTION 6. That this Ordinance is declared to be an emergency measure and shall take effect and be in force from and after its passage. The reason for the emergency lies in the fact that this Ordinance is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety and property, and for the further reason that this Ordinance must be immediately effective in order to facilitate the Plant Pumps, Motors & Valves Rebuild/Replacement Project at the Water Reclamation Facility.

..Body
SUMMARY & BACKGROUND:
The Divisions of Road and Bridge Maintenance and Government Affairs have successfully applied for and received funding from the Ohio Emergency Management Agency (OEMA), administering Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) funding secured by Rep. Kaptur through Community Project Funding, and the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR), administering state capital funding, to restore the North Summit Street Embankment that sustained storm damage. This project will reconstruct the embankment and multi-use path between the Point Place lighthouse and Cullen Park and is part of the larger Summit Riverfront Corridor project to connect Point Place to downtown. The city of Toledo will administer the construction of the project. Matching funds have been authorized through the Division of Road and Bridge Maintenance 2026 Matches and Planning fund. Construction is expected to begin in 2027 through 2028.  

..Summary
NOW THEREFORE Be it ordained by the Council of the City of Toledo:

SECTION 1. SECTION 2. SECTION 3. SECTION 4. Contracts shall contain such terms and conditions as the Mayor may deem requisite and proper and shall be subject to approval by the Director of Transportation and the Director of Law.

SECTION 5.  That the Finance Director is authorized to draw their warrant or warrants against the Account Codes identified above in an amount not to exceed those authorized above in payment of the obligations incurred pursuant to the contracts authorized in Section 4 upon presentation of the proper voucher or vouchers.

	SECTION 6.  That this Ordinance is declared to be an emergency measure and shall be in force and effect from and after its passage.  The reason for the emergency lies in the fact that this Ordinance is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety and property, and for the further reason that this Ordinance must be immediately effective in order to facilitate the planning and construction of the North Summit Street Embankment Stabilization Project.
